ns2:course.label: Dancing Techniques III
ns2:course.description: A progressive exploration from DANC 260 of varied movement practices designed to support the dance major's ability to ARTICULATE their creative evolution. This daily practice of technique teaches the student to perform with clarity, versatility, and personal style, preparing students for the physical rigor associated with a performing career in dance. To provide a balance of training from a range of Africanist and Europeanist cultural origins, this course will include 2-3 contemporary movement approaches per semester, which may include techniques such as Ballet, Contemporary Modern, Improvisation, West African, Umfundalai, Hip-hop, House, Jazz, Capoeira, Tap. Specific dance forms for each semester will be listed in the class schedule. May be repeated in separate terms. Prerequisite: Passing grade in two semesters of DANC 260. For Dance majors only or by consent of instructor. Non-dance majors admitted by audition on a space-available basis.
